about.title: Placentia Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Placentia sees hundreds of injury collisions each year along corridors like SR-57, Orangethorpe Avenue, and Placentia Avenue, and even one fatal crash reshapes a family's life. Under California law, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges the driver might face, and it exists to help surviving spouses, domestic partners, children, or in some cases other dependents recover the financial and emotional losses tied to that death. These claims can address funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance. Because California limits who has legal standing to bring this type of claim, and because the filing window is generally two years from the date of death — shorter if a government entity is involved — it helps to talk with someone who understands these rules early. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can walk through the options at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You File

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California law gives standing first to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and only in their absence to other dependents or heirs. An attorney can confirm who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Generally Two Years
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter notice period. Missing these windows can end a family's ability to recover anything at all.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, along with compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the deceased provided. These claims are civil matters, separate from any criminal proceedings against the at-fault driver.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Placentia?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government agency, such as a public road authority, may share fault, the deadline for filing a notice is much shorter, often just six months. An attorney can confirm the exact timeline that applies to your family's situation.

items.question: Can we file if the fatal crash happened on SR-57 or another state highway near Placentia?
items.answer: Yes, the location of the crash doesn't change who has standing to file, though it may affect whether a government entity is a potential party. Crashes on state highways sometimes involve road design or maintenance questions that an attorney would need to evaluate separately from driver fault.

items.question: What if our loved one didn't have a spouse or children?
items.answer: California law then allows certain other dependents or heirs to bring the claim, depending on the family structure. This is one of the more nuanced areas of wrongful death law, so it's worth discussing your specific situation with an attorney rather than assuming who qualifies.
